# The result of a fold of maxima of two limbs: one step above the maximum, or NaN

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `norm_finish_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The result of a fold of maxima from its final state, the largest magnitude $m$ and the mask $\mathit{ok}$ that no element was a NaN: $\mathrm{succ}(m)$ when $\mathit{ok}$ is true and it is finite, with the flag $\mathit{flag}$ true; otherwise a NaN and the flag false (the canonical NaN of [When something is not finite](../developer/design/milestone2.md#sum-dot-axpy-convolution)):

$$r = \mathrm{succ}(m) \ \text{when } \mathit{ok} \text{ is true and } \mathrm{succ}(m) \text{ is finite}, \qquad r = \mathrm{NaN} \text{ otherwise}.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of the loop `norm_upper_2`, called by `norm_upper` of `SoAView<const T, 2>` ([Functions on arrays](batch.md)) and of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)).

## Requires

- $m$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $\mathit{ok}$ is a mask, true or false.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $\mathit{flag}$ is true exactly when $\mathit{ok}$ is true and $\mathrm{succ}(m)$ is finite.
- When it is, $r = \mathrm{succ}(m)$.
- Otherwise $r$ is a NaN.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `norm_finish_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeFoldNorm.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeFoldNorm.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions norm_finish_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `norm_finish_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the finish of a fold of maxima: the step after the maximum, or the canonical NaN (milestone2.md). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/norm_finish_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/norm_finish_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`fold_finish_1`](fold_finish_1.md).

```
# The finish of norm_upper_2 (milestone2.md, "sum, dot, axpy, convolution": norm_upper_k; "When
# something is not finite"): one step up from the largest magnitude of a leading limb, which is at
# least the magnitude of every element (normalized_2_between) and at most one step above the
# smallest number of the format not below the largest of them, when no element was a NaN (the mask
# ok) and that step is finite, with the flag true; otherwise the canonical NaN and the flag false.
# The step from the largest finite number is infinite: an array of finite elements whose largest
# leading limb is the largest finite number in magnitude gives the flag false, as does an element
# that is not finite.

s         = succ(m)
t         = select(ok, s, const nan)
(r, flag) = fold_finish_1(t)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#norm_finish_2)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 1 991 824 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
